title: Padded satin stitch
subtitle: Satin stitch worked over a raised foundation for a sculptural, domed surface
excerpt: Padded satin stitch layers a padding foundation beneath the final satin stitches to raise the surface and give the shape a rounded, sculptural appearance. The padding can be straight stitches, chain stitch, or felt cutouts. The satin stitch on top covers the padding completely.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), padded embroidery chapter (Project Gutenberg #20776). Weldon's Practical Needlework, Vol. 3 (1887), raised satin stitch entry.

glossaryTerms.definition: A layer of stitches worked first, in a direction opposite to the final surface stitches, to build up the fabric surface and create a rounded, raised effect when the final layer covers them.

before the final satin stitches are added. The padding is usually straight stitches running perpendicular to the final satin direction, or a layer of chain stitch filling. The final satin stitches run over the padding, smoothing it into a raised dome.

items.label: Padding thread
items.value: Stranded cotton 4 to 6 strands for the foundation

items.label: Satin thread
items.value: Stranded cotton 3 to 4 strands or silk

content.text: Work split stitch or back stitch around the shape outline to give a firm edge.
Fill the shape with straight stitches running perpendicular to the final satin direction. Pack them closely.
Work a second padding layer if more height is needed, this time running parallel to the final satin direction.
Cover the padding with satin stitches at the chosen angle, keeping them smooth and parallel.

items.fix: Pack the satin stitches tightly enough to cover the padding completely. Use the same thread weight for satin as for padding.
items.cause: Satin stitches are spaced too widely.
items.symptom: The padding shows through the satin layer

items.fix: Always work split stitch around the edge first. The satin stitches taken to the split stitch edge produce a crisp, raised border.
